title: LLM traffic kinematics & slice activation playbook (WIP)
content:
Purpose
This is a working playbook for how we choreograph traffic movement (kinematics) and slice activation for LLM features during cross-functional releases. Focus: make microreleases predictable for latency/cost-sensitive inference features while preserving behavioral safety (hallucination, toxicity) and experiment integrity.

Scope
- Applies to Hosted API and Dedicated deployments; private deployments follow same choreography but may require additional network change windows.
- Covers: staged canaries, A/B allocations, slice activation, safety gating, telemetry checks, and rollback paths.
- Not a replacement for incident runbooks; this assumes normal-release path.

Key definitions (quick)
- slice: logically grouped user cohort (by geography, product surface, customer tier, or signal).
- microrelease: small exposure increment (0.1% to 5%) used to validate safety and perf before broad rollout.
- steward: person responsible for observability during a microrelease (rotates per release).
- activation window: scheduled time block with full comms + oncall overlap.

High-level choreography (one-line)
1) Prep (0–48h): tests, synthetic traffic, and baseline telemetry snapshot.
2) Stage canary (0.1% slice) for 30–60m: smoke perf + behavioral checks.
3) Expand to micro cohorts (1%, 5%) with hold points.
4) Run A/B (if experiment) for statistical power or proceed to rollout if safety signals are green.
5) Full activation and post-mortem.

Pre-release checklist (owner: release lead)
- Confirm model version pin and fallback variant (e.g., quantized, smaller-context).
- Deploy to a staging cluster and run 1000 synthetic prompts matching production distribution. Capture latency, 99p, mem spikes.
- Prepare synthetic hallucination probes (50 canonical prompts + adversarial variants).
- Identify steward and oncall coverage. Add names to release calendar.
- Ensure canary traffic routing rule exists in Console and code repo (brief snippet): route->model:vX if cohort==canary.
- Create JIRA ticket with experiment metrics and hypothesis. Link to this doc.

Activation timeline (suggested)
- T0: push config to route traffic 0.1% -> new model. Start steward watch.
- T0+30m: if perf and safety green, increase to 1%.
- T0+90m: if still green, increase to 5% and start A/B collection window (if applicable) for at least one business cycle (min 4–6 hrs depending on metric SNR).
- T+post: decision point — proceed/rollback/pause.

Signal categories and example thresholds (tunable)
- Performance: 99th latency increase > 20% vs baseline OR p95 > SLA -> pause.
- Errors: model error rate (runtime failures) > 0.5% absolute increase -> rollback.
- Cost: cost-per-1000-tokens increases > 50% -> review (possible quantized variant).
- Behavioral: hallucination score (eval harness) delta > 3% absolute OR safety filter hit rate increases > 1.5x -> pause + manual review.
- Business metrics: conversion / downstream task success drop with p < 0.05 -> pause and investigate.
- Telemetry spike heuristics: sudden drop in requests for a slice (>30%) or spike in retries -> investigate routing/latency.

Telemetry queries / quick checks (examples)
- P95 latency by slice over last 30m: SELECT slice, percentile(latency_ms,95) FROM requests WHERE model='vX' GROUP BY slice
- Hallucination probe failures (synthetic): count where ground_truth_match=false AND model='vX'
- Cost delta: (tokens_vX_cost - tokens_baseline_cost) / tokens_baseline_cost
Note: these are placeholders; Console will show exact query templates in Metrics > Rollouts.

A/B design considerations
- Randomization: ensure sampling keyed by user-id (deterministic) to avoid cross-contamination and reallocation jitter.
- Exposure freeze: once a user is assigned to an experiment, keep them constant until experiment end or forced reassign.
- Power calc: for low-signal business metrics, use longer windows or larger slices; for behavior metrics (hallucination) synthetic probes may yield faster signal.

Safety gating flow (behavioral + perf)
1) Automated gates run at each hold point (0.1%,1%,5%). If any gate trips -> immediate pause and steward notifies product + SRE + ML owners.
2) Triage: steward runs the quick investigation checklist (logs, sample responses, model logits if available).
3) Remediation: if root cause is model drift or prompt handling, revert traffic to fallback variant. If infra cause -> file follow-up with infra/SRE.
4) Communication: update the release Jira, ping #release-ops and the release thread with a 1–2 line summary.

Rollback matrix (examples)
- Perf regression only: route back to baseline, keep new model artifact for offline debug, label release as partial-failure.
- Safety regression: full rollback, deprioritize for A/B until model/filters fixed. Create post-mortem.
- Instrumentation gap discovered: pause expansion, increase logging and synthetic probes, re-run T0 after fixes.

Human-in-the-loop checks (when to require)
- If behavioral gate trips at 0.1% -> require manual signoff from ML lead before resuming.
- If business metric impact is ambiguous but close to threshold -> run side-by-side golden set evaluation for 24h.

Comms templates (short)
- Slack (release-ops): "Rolling vX -> canary (0.1%) now. Steward: @Ethan. Watch p95, errors, halluc probe. Links: <metrics> <jira>."
- Incident-ish: "Pausing vX rollout due to spike in hallucination probe failures. Reverted to vW. Investigating. See JIRA-1245."

Experiment logging & artifacts (what to attach to JIRA)
- Baseline snapshots (latency, cost, safety rates) for 24h pre-release.
- Synthetic probe results with example failure responses.
- Traffic allocation timeline and steward notes (who observed what and when).
- Metric queries used and raw CSV exports.

Operational tips & heuristics (from field)
- Start tiny and measure early — behavioral signals often show up faster than downstream business impact.
- Use synthetic adversarial prompts to stress hallucination; real-user signals and synthetic probes are complementary.
- Keep a cheap fallback (smaller model/shorter context) for instant rollback to preserve UX while debugging.
- Prefer increasing slices in multiples of 5x (0.1 -> 0.5 -> 2.5 -> 12.5) only if steady cadence is needed; sometimes 0.1 -> 1 -> 5 is simpler.

Open questions (to resolve before finalizing template)
- Granularity of steward rotation for overlapping releases (can one steward cover two unrelated microreleases?)
- Exact default thresholds for hallucination metrics — need to standardize across model families.
- How long to keep synthetic probe history for trend detection?

Next steps (owner: Priya)
- Turn this into a Console template: automatic deployment checklist + gating config.
- Sync with SRE to add an alert runbook for sudden retry spikes during rollouts.
- Run a dry-run on next staging cut with synthetic noise to validate timing assumptions.

Notes to self
- This doc intentionally light on exact SQL / query syntax; steal the metric names from Metrics > Rollouts when building the Console template.
- Keep a short cheat-sheet for stewards with 5 commands they should run in the first 15 minutes.

---
If anything here looks opinionated or missing, flag in the release thread or drop a comment in JIRA-1245.
